full_zh: 背景：团队有几十张对账表，每一张都有自己手写的校验 task，所以每加一张表就要写、评审、发布一个新 task，成本很高。
问题：我想让加检查变便宜，并且让 is this data safe to read 变成一个硬条件，而不是 Slack 里的约定。

我做了什么：我做了一张配置表，一行就说明哪个 subject area 跑哪个存储过程、SLA 是什么；一个通用 executor 用动态 SQL 调用并写入标准化的 PASS / FAIL / WARNING，exception handler 把崩溃变成 FAIL 行，所以一个坏检查不会拖垮其他检查；全部检查通过后状态行翻成 Completed 并复制到 share 层，下游 JOIN 它。我自己铺开了 8 个 subject area，加检查变成插入一行。

结果：之后我在生产规模下发现自己设计的缺陷：就绪判断按表，约 50 个持续失败的商户挡住了 35000 个商户。我没有悄悄修补，而是写了 ADR：四个方案加正确性论证和容量分析，否决 VARIANT（关闭谓词下推）、flatten（单元格大小上限）和新表（新基础设施），选了汇总行加每商户失败行，规则是 strictest wins。当前状态要说准：框架和 8 次铺开已在生产，商户级就绪已设计、评审，并在一个 subject area 验证过，全框架铺开排在 net settlement 之后。
为什么这样做 / 学到：粒度是随规模要重新审视的设计参数；修自己的缺陷也应走正式的 ADR；设计任何 gate 之前先问一个检查失败时的 blast radius 是谁。
full_en: Our team had dozens of reconciliation tables, and every new one got its own hand-written validation task. I replaced that with a config-driven quality-check framework. One row in a config table says which stored procedure to run for which subject area, with what SLA. A generic executor builds the call, captures the result, and writes a normalized pass, fail or warning row, and an exception handler means one broken check never takes down the others. When every enabled check passes, a status row flips to Completed and replicates to a share layer where downstream teams JOIN on it. So 'is this data safe to read' went from a Slack convention to a SQL condition. I rolled it out across eight subject areas myself, and adding a check became inserting a row. Then I saw a flaw in my own design: readiness was per table, so roughly fifty bad merchants out of thirty-five thousand blocked everybody. I didn't patch it quietly. I wrote an ADR with four alternatives, a correctness argument, and a volume analysis. The direction is reviewed and proven in one subject area; the broader rollout is sequenced behind the net-settlement work.

full.example: I made validation config-driven, so adding a check is inserting a row instead of shipping a task.
Downstream teams treat the status row as a quality gate and JOIN on it.

full.en: own up to a flaw in my own design
full.zh: 主动承认自己设计里的缺陷
full.example: I owned up to a flaw in my own design and wrote an ADR instead of patching it quietly.

hook.example: The granularity flaw only showed up at scale, with fifty bad merchants blocking thirty-five thousand.
Roughly four percent of merchants, about fifty, were blocking everyone else.
Storing only failures keeps the worst case around eight hundred thousand rows a month.

starl.example: The status table decouples downstream readers from how each check is implemented.
The replicated status row became the single source of truth for whether data is safe to read.

starl.en: make the right thing the easy thing
starl.zh: 让正确的做法成为最省事的做法
starl.example: Insert-a-row onboarding made the right thing the easy thing for every subject area.

followups.example: Strictest wins means a table-level failure always blocks, so mixed deployments stay safe.
A per-row UDF over a secure view turns off predicate pushdown, which is why I rejected the VARIANT option.
An unconverted procedure degrades gracefully to today's table-level blocking.

relp.zh: 主动去证伪自己的假设
relp.example: I tried to disconfirm my own abstraction the way I would review someone else's code.

relp.en: build a platform, not a feature
relp.zh: 做平台而不是单个功能
relp.example: I built a platform, not a feature, so other teams could plug checks in.
I stay transparent about status: the ADR direction is proven in one area, not rolled out everywhere.

senior.q: How did you decide the granularity of readiness should be per merchant rather than per table?
senior.why: 面试官在探：你有没有用数据和成本论证一个设计粒度，而不是凭感觉。
framework: 先给事实：约 50 个持续失败的商户挡住 35000 个商户，也就是约 4%
再比较方案：VARIANT 会关闭谓词下推，flatten 会受单元格大小上限限制，新表要新基础设施
再说选择：汇总行加每商户失败行，复用现有结果表
最后说容量：只存失败行，极端情况每月约 80 万行
senior.best_practice: 粒度选错的代价随规模放大，所以要用生产数据量化被误伤的范围。每个被否决的方案都用具体机制说明为什么不行，这样结论经得起别人复核。选复用现有表是因为零新基础设施，上线风险最低。

terms.example: I quantified the impact first: fifty bad merchants against thirty-five thousand healthy ones.
The capacity analysis showed that storing only failures costs about eight hundred thousand rows a month.

senior.q: How would you roll out the merchant-level change safely across all eight subject areas?
senior.why: 面试官在探：你对灰度和回退是否有清晰的方法，而不是一次性全推。
framework: 先说顺序：已在一个 subject area 验证过，再按风险从低到高逐个改造
再说兼容：strictest wins 保证改造过和没改造的 procedure 混跑也是安全的
再说验证：新旧读结果在同一批数据上对比，差异必须能解释
最后说回退：每个 area 单独可退，退回就是今天的表级行为
senior.best_practice: strictest wins 让每个 subject area 可以独立迁移，混跑时最坏也只是退化成表级阻塞，所以不需要停机窗口或一次性切换。逐个迁移配合新旧结果对比，能在影响面最小时发现问题。这也是我把全框架铺开排在 net settlement 之后的原因，不让两件大事同时进行。

terms.example: I would do an incremental rollout, one subject area at a time, each independently reversible.
Strictest wins keeps the change backward compatible with unconverted procedures.

senior.q: What are the risks of dynamic SQL in a framework other teams plug into, and how do you control them?
senior.why: 面试官在探：你是否认识到平台的风险面，并有现实的缓解措施。
framework: 先说威胁模型：配置经 migration 受控，不是用户输入，所以注入不是主要风险
再说真风险：失去静态检查，配置写错要到运行时才知道
再说缓解：exception handler 把崩溃变成 FAIL 行，结果表加健康检查
最后说治理：谁能改配置、怎么评审，要像改代码一样严格
senior.best_practice: 判断风险要先定威胁模型，否则会把力气花在不存在的威胁上。动态 SQL 的真代价是错误延后到运行时，所以要用异常处理和对结果表本身的监控把错误尽快暴露。配置进了 migration，改动就有评审和记录。

terms.example: Config goes through migrations, so in my threat model injection is not the main risk.
The exception handler is a guardrail so one bad config row can't take down other checks.

senior.q: How would you tell whether other teams are actually adopting the framework, and what would you do if they were not?
senior.why: 面试官在探：你对平台采用度怎么衡量，以及是否会倾听使用者。
framework: 先说指标：由别人插入的配置行数、接入的 subject area 数、下游 JOIN 它的消费者数
再说定性：直接问接入的人卡在哪里，是文档、权限还是接口
再说行动：把最常见的卡点做成模板或脚本，降低第一次接入的成本
最后说诚实：目前最强的证据是别人不问我就加了一行，没有就不声称
senior.best_practice: 平台成功的标准是别人在不找你的情况下用起来，所以要看别人自己加的配置行，而不是自己的铺开次数。把卡点前移到文档和模板，是为了让第一次接入的成本足够低。不夸大采用度，也是 Earn Trust 的一部分。

terms.example: My adoption metric would be check rows added by other people without asking me.
I would reduce friction with a template for the most common onboarding case.
